Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

pollinatoR 0.4.0

Breaking changes

  • The default delta interval of pollin_effects() on a glmmTMB fit is now taken over the fixed and random effects jointly, with their covariance from the inverse of the joint precision of the Laplace approximation. The estimand averages over the trial’s own blocks and slopes, and the previous interval held those at their modes, so it was too wide wherever the estimand depends on them: on designs with a random treatment slope and under a logit link. On a log link without a slope the interval is unchanged. pollin_contribution() and the simulation draws of pollin_draws() (and so pollin_value()) use the same covariance, and the glmmTMB intervals of pollin_cate() draw the fixed effects and the slopes jointly.
  • interval = "delta_fixed" gives the interval of 0.3.1 and earlier, on pollin_effects() and pollin_contribution().
  • Delta estimates now equal the G-computation used everywhere else in the package. The 0.3.1 estimate came from marginaleffects and differed from it by up to about 1e-5 relative; "delta_fixed" keeps the old numbers.

New behaviour

  • When the joint precision is singular, as with a variance estimated at zero, the interval holds the variance parameters at their estimates and a warning says so. A zero-inflated fit is refused, with a pointer to the bootstrap.
  • TMB and Matrix, both already required by glmmTMB, join Imports.

Validation

  • On 800 simulated trials over six designs, the joint interval covers the planted effect 0.930 to 0.970 of the time and is as wide as the flexyBayes posterior (median width ratio 0.98 to 1.00). On the same data the 0.3.1 interval was 1.3 to 1.9 times wider on the binomial and random-slope designs and covered 0.98 to 1.00.

pollinatoR 0.3.1

The flexyBayes engine is no longer labelled experimental. Its posterior on designs with a random treatment slope matches an exact posterior, and the remaining coverage shortfall on those designs is a property of the interval with few sites (see Validation).

Bug fixes

  • pollin_data(denominator = ) now reaches the fit. Each response is a count of successes out of the denominator’s trials (seeds out of ovules, pods out of flowers) and is fitted as binomial with a logit link: cbind(response, denominator - response) on glmmTMB, and one 0/1 row per trial on flexyBayes, which takes no trials argument. The arm means of pollin_effects() and pollin_draws() are expected proportions, averaged over the original rows with equal weight whatever their number of trials, as for every other response. The delta, bootstrap, simulation and posterior paths all take the binomial fit, and the posterior draws are averaged over the original rows. pollin_contribution() fits the same way; pollin_moderation() still models the count itself.
  • With a denominator, family = NULL picks binomial(); any other family is an error that names the family, the response and the denominator. The response must be a whole number between 0 and the denominator and the denominator positive on the rows fitted; a row with a missing denominator is dropped, and a row with a denominator of 0 is an error. On flexyBayes, an expansion beyond two million trial rows is an error that points to the glmmTMB engine.
  • Data that declared a denominator were fitted as the count itself up to 0.3.0. They are now fitted as binomial, so their estimates change, and data whose counts exceed the denominator stop.
  • sn joins Suggests. INLA needs it, and without it a package check run with flexyBayes and INLA installed failed on the pollin_cate() example.

Validation

  • On the 12-site design with a random treatment slope, where 0.3.0 found posterior 95% coverage of 0.909 to 0.925, coverage stays at 0.910 under every setting reachable through flexyBayes: hyperparameters fixed at their mode or integrated on a finer grid, and three other variance priors. With the hyperparameters fixed at their planted values, INLA and an exact Stan (NUTS) posterior both cover 0.930, with widths within 1% (validation/probe_S3.1_slope_coverage.md).
  • A re-test on new seeds (validation/planted_truth_S3.1_report.md) did not meet its criteria in full. On binomial counts with a denominator the posterior covers 0.960, and the engines agree on the estimate in every trial, but the width criterion fails (ratio 0.756) because the glmmTMB delta interval is wider than it needs to be (coverage 0.985). On the Poisson control the posterior covers 0.980, one trial past the 0.97 band edge; glmmTMB covers 0.980 on the same trials. The negative binomial deficit control passes (0.940).

Known limitations

  • On a binomial ratio with a logit link, the glmmTMB delta interval over-covers: it treats the block effects as known while the intercept, which does not cancel from the ratio on the logit scale, varies.
  • The glmmTMB delta estimate can differ from the G-computation of predict() by about 1e-6, because marginaleffects reads the random effects at the last state glmmTMB evaluated.

pollinatoR 0.3.0

This release adds a Bayesian engine and per-level effects with partial pooling. A fit made through flexyBayes on INLA gives posterior draws, and effects, populations, values and guards take them as they take the glmmTMB draws. The vignette Bayesian fits with flexyBayes compares the two engines. The flexyBayes engine is experimental in this release; the validation below says where its intervals are and are not calibrated.

New features

  • pollin_fit(engine = "flexyBayes") fits each response with flexyBayes::flexybayes() on INLA, with the fixed part of the glmmTMB engine and the design’s random terms. The families nbinom2(), poisson(), binomial(), Gamma(link = "log") and beta_family() are mapped to the flexyBayes families negative_binomial, poisson, binomial, gamma and beta, with their log or logit links. Priors pass through ... as written. flexyBayes and INLA are suggested packages, and the extension API version of flexyBayes is checked when the fit is made.
  • pollin_draws(method = "posterior"), the default and only method for a flexyBayes fit, draws the fixed effects, random effects and variance parameters jointly from the posterior and recomputes the arm means per draw by the G-computation rule of the glmmTMB engine. With a seed, which sets both R’s generator and INLA’s, the draws repeat exactly.
  • pollin_effects(interval = "posterior"), the default for a flexyBayes fit, reports the posterior median, standard deviation and equal-tailed interval of the estimand, with p.value NA. New argument n_draws.
  • pollin_cate() reports the contrast at each level of a column with a random treatment slope, partially pooled towards the overall effect. The column is the design’s slope unit (pollin_design(slope = )) or one declared with the new pollin_fit(pooled = ). On flexyBayes the estimate and interval come from the posterior draws. The print points to the unpooled per-level contrasts, from a fit with by and no slope, read with pollin_effects().

Validation

  • Planted-truth simulations, 200 trials per cell (100 for per-level effects), compare the engines and check posterior coverage (validation/planted_truth_S3_report.md). None of the three pre-set criteria is met in full:
    • The two engines agree on the estimate (within 0.25 glmmTMB standard errors) in 97% to 100% of trials in every cell. On designs with a random treatment slope, glmmTMB stops at a variance on its boundary in 4% to 12% of trials; flexyBayes fits every trial.
    • Posterior 95% intervals cover 0.945 to 0.960 on designs with unit intercepts (negative binomial, Poisson, deficit) and 0.932 to 0.939 on the overall effect of pooled fits, but 0.909 to 0.925 on designs with a site slope, and 0.925 on a binary response. On slope designs the glmmTMB delta interval over-covers (0.989 to 1.000) at about 1.7 times the posterior width.
    • pollin_cate() lowers the error of per-level effects by 12% to 15% on average against unpooled contrasts, but does better in only 69% to 79% of trials, against a 90% target. Posterior per-level coverage is 0.940 to 0.941.

Known limitations

  • The flexyBayes engine is experimental: its intervals run slightly narrow on designs with a random treatment slope (see Validation).
  • pollin_data(denominator = ) does not reach the fit on either engine, so a count out of a known number of trials (seeds out of ovules) cannot yet be fitted as binomial; one 0/1 row per trial works.
  • flexyBayes on INLA does not fit a correlated random treatment slope. The flexyBayes engine fits a unit intercept plus an independent unit-by-arm effect instead, a restricted form of glmmTMB’s unstructured slope: equal variances across arms and a non-negative correlation between them.
  • The brms backend of flexyBayes is refused, because posterior draws of a brms fit are not in the flexyBayes extension API version 1. Families other than the five above, Tweedie among them, are refused by name.
  • On glmmTMB, pollin_cate() intervals are approximate. The fixed effects and the slope coefficients are drawn independently, since glmmTMB gives the conditional variance of each coefficient on its own. When the slope variance is estimated at zero, pollin_cate() stops.

pollinatoR 0.2.0

This release adds economic valuation. A fitted estimand can be scaled to a population of fields and turned into a value with an interval, computed draw by draw. Every value prints its basis, population, price year, currency and source.

Breaking changes

  • pollin_spec() is removed, as announced in 0.1.0, with its print method. pollin_contribution(), pollin_moderation() and pollin_validate() no longer accept a pollin_spec and take only the layered objects. The getting-started vignette shows the equivalent calls.

New features

  • pollin_draws() returns draws of the two arm means of a fitted estimand and of the estimand formed from them, on its scale and basis. The default method = "simulation" draws the fixed effects from their sampling distribution and covers fixed-effect uncertainty, as the delta interval does. method = "bootstrap" uses the parametric bootstrap refits of pollin_effects() and gives the same interval. summary() gives the median and percentile interval per column.
  • pollin_population() declares a population of strata, the levels of one column (distance bands, regions, varieties) weighted by area, and pollin_estimand(population = ) accepts it. The fit is made with the strata as by, and pollin_draws() adds a "population" column. The population estimand is formed from the area-weighted arm means: a ratio of population means, not a weighted mean of the stratum estimands. pollin_effects() reports the trial contrasts and does not use the population.
  • pollin_market() declares current production and price, as scalars or with draws, with the unit, currency, price year and a source that prints with every value.
  • pollin_value() multiplies draws of an estimand by price and production. The channel has no default:
    • "dependence" takes a loss share and gives the value lost under total exclusion of pollinators;
    • "deficit" takes the gain of hand pollination over open and gives the value of closing that gap.
    Each channel accepts only its own estimand. A gain offered to the dependence channel is refused, since g = D / (1 - D) overstates the loss by 1 / (1 - D). A descriptive index or a plain number is refused because it has no estimand. Market draws are matched to the estimand draws by position.
  • pollin_guard_doublecount() adds values draw by draw and stops when two of them count the same pollination within a crop: a part plus its total, the same pollinators twice, two products of one crop (seed and oil), or two named guilds. For guilds, nested = FALSE confirms that they come from separate, non-nested exclusions, and the statement prints with the total. Each value records the pollinators removed (pollin_value(agent = ), "all" by default), the product and the crop (pollin_market(crop = )).
  • New vignette From dependence to value. A matched-pair field study gains a section on scaling the estimand from the sampled fields to a growing area.

Validation

  • Golden-value tests check that the 0.1.0 outputs are unchanged: deficit and dependence on every scale, with delta and bootstrap intervals, overall and by level, and the contribution, moderation, validation and index results (validation/golden/make_golden_v0.1.0.R).
  • Planted-truth calibration of value intervals over 1,000 simulated trials per cell (three-arm, split-plot and matched-pair designs, both channels, market inputs fixed or drawn, one two-stratum population): 95% interval coverage between 0.937 and 0.962 in all 11 cells. The bias criterion (below 0.1 standard errors) holds in 9 of 11; see Known limitations (validation/planted_truth_S2_report.md).
  • The published valuation of Yocgo et al. (2023, Scientific Reports 13:20108) is reproduced from its supplementary data: totals to the dollar and all 20 published figures within their rounding (validation/value_oracle/).

Known limitations

  • pollin_contribution(by = ) stops with “jacobian does not match the variance-covariance matrix” on nested multi-site data where the by variable is constant within the slope unit.
  • The value summary is the median of the value draws. On the dependence channel with market draws it sits slightly low, by 0.13 to 0.14 standard errors in two planted-truth cells, because the loss share is concave in the log ratio and the median of a product falls below the product of medians. Interval coverage is unaffected.
  • Simulation draws cover fixed-effect uncertainty only. Use method = "bootstrap" when the random effects should vary as well.
  • A value assumes no price response, a total-loss counterfactual for the dependence channel, and independence of the estimand and market draws. It is gross revenue, before costs.

pollinatoR 0.1.0

An analysis is now declared in layers: the data (pollin_data()), the design (pollin_design()) and the estimand (pollin_estimand()), then fitted (pollin_fit()) and read on the estimand’s scale (pollin_effects()).

Breaking changes

  • The first argument of pollin_validate(), pollin_contribution() and pollin_moderation() is renamed from spec to x. Calls that pass it by position are unaffected.
  • pollin_contribution() takes a pollin_estimand with family = "dependence" and scale = "difference". Its table carries the columns of pollin_effects() plus slope_sd and p.fdr. With by, it fits the treatment-by-level interaction and reports each level’s own contrast. A pollin_spec with by is fitted as before.
  • pollin_moderation() takes a pollin_design whose data declare exposures. The default of exposures is now NULL, meaning every declared exposure.
  • pollin_spec() is deprecated and is removed at version 0.2.0. It warns once per session. pollin_contribution(), pollin_moderation() and pollin_validate() still accept a pollin_spec until then.
  • Removed six unused packages from Suggests (DHARMa, emmeans, brms, boot, fst, data.table).

New features

  • pollin_data() declares the unit-of-record table: response, treatment, unit nesting, and optional grouping, denominator, exposure and adjustment columns. Roles are checked against the data and the structural checks are stored with the object.
  • pollin_design() declares the arms (excluded, open, supplemented), the layout (crd, rcbd, split_plot, matched_pairs, multi_site) and the reference arm. The layout sets the random structure; a random treatment slope sits on the site in multi_site and is opt-in elsewhere through slope. Units lacking an arm are counted in a warning.
  • pollin_estimand() names the estimand: deficit (supplemented versus open) or dependence (excluded versus the reference arm), on the difference, ratio, RII or lnRR scale. basis ("loss" or "gain") has no default, so a loss share cannot be read as a gain. pollin_assumptions() lists the assumptions the estimand rests on for its layout.
  • pollin_fit() fits one glmmTMB model per response, with the treatment as the fixed effect and the design’s random terms. The family is chosen from each response’s values unless given, singly or per response. With by, the fixed part is treatment * by, so each level of by has its own treatment effect.
  • pollin_effects() reports the estimand on its declared scale from averaged model predictions (a ratio of expected values, never a mean of unit ratios), with a delta interval computed on the log-ratio scale and transformed, so a loss share stays below 1 and the RII inside (-1, 1), or with a parametric bootstrap interval (interval = "bootstrap", n_boot, seed). Every table records the family, scale and basis. Per-level contrasts come from a fit made with by; asking for a by the fit was not made with is an error. The printed result states that delta intervals cover fixed-effect uncertainty only.
  • pollin_index() and pollin_rii() accept a pollin_design and work from unit-level arm means; pollin_compensation() accepts a pollin_data and uses its responses as the components. The vector and data-frame interfaces are unchanged and return the same numbers.
  • pollin_guard_bounded() refuses to average unit-level RII or dependence values unless allow = TRUE, and reports the index of the arm means beside the average.
  • pollin_guard_ecological() splits an exposure into between-unit and within-unit parts and warns when an exposure slope exists only between units, or when the two slopes disagree in sign.
  • pollin_guard_posttreatment() stops when an adjustment covariate is among the variables the user declares to be downstream of the treatment.
  • New vignettes: A three-arm trial: deficit and dependence, A split-plot trial: dependence by variety and A matched-pair field study. The getting-started vignette is rewritten around the layered workflow.

Known limitations

  • In the planted-truth recovery study (validation/planted_truth_S1_report.md), 24 of 25 design-by-estimand cells meet the pre-set rule. The matched-pair dependence estimate on the difference scale is biased by -0.19 standard errors; its interval coverage (0.950) and the ratio-scale estimates pass. For matched-pair designs the ratio scale is the better-supported report.

Moving from earlier calls

Before Now
pollin_spec(data, outcomes, treatment, control, random) pollin_data(data, response, treatment, unit) then pollin_design(x, arms = c(excluded = control, open = ...), layout)
pollin_spec(..., latent_unit = "Site") pollin_design(..., layout = "multi_site"), or slope = "Site" with another layout
pollin_spec(..., exposures, adjust) pollin_data(..., exposures, adjust)
pollin_contribution(spec) pollin_contribution(pollin_estimand(design, "dependence", "difference", basis = "loss"))
Any other scale or interval pollin_effects(pollin_fit(estimand))
pollin_contribution(spec, by = "Region") pollin_effects(pollin_fit(estimand, by = "Region")), now one fixed treatment effect per region
pollin_moderation(spec, outcome) pollin_moderation(design, outcome)
pollin_validate(spec) pollin_validate(pollin_data(...)), also run when the object is built
pollin_index(open_means, cage_means) Unchanged, or pollin_index(design, response)

pollinatoR 0.0.0.9000

  • Initial development scaffold.
  • pollin_spec() declares an exclusion-experiment study (outcomes, treatment, nested random structure, exposures, adjustment, latent grouping).
  • pollin_contribution() estimates the per-outcome pollinator contribution (open minus exclusion) as a model-based average treatment effect with propagated uncertainty, carrying a random treatment slope on the latent unit to absorb unobserved between-unit (e.g. genotype) heterogeneity.
  • pollin_moderation() estimates how the contribution varies with exposures (treatment-by-exposure conditional effects) using a within-between decomposition so the within-unit estimate is robust to site-level confounders.
  • pollin_index() / pollin_rii() provide uncertainty-aware dependence indices, including the Relative Interaction Index with a bootstrap interval.
  • pollin_guard_spurious() tests an index-versus-yield slope against a permutation null that isolates the mechanical (shared-term) coupling.
  • pollin_validate() runs structural and internal-consistency integrity checks.
  • pollin_compensation() summarises yield-component trade-offs.
